digest.component_or_area: comment synchronization and reconciler binding state
propositions: Comment identity is currently fragile, relying on normalized body-text equality which collides on duplicate bodies and cannot track edited comments; stable identity must use a persistent local-comment-key (HLC timestamp) to Jira-comment-ID map as the primary guard.

The returned Jira comment ID from add_comment() is currently discarded at both create and update enactment sites, preventing durable capture of the mapping; the ID must be captured and immediately persisted in binding_store via record_comment_id() at both sites, requiring binding_store to be threaded through the update call chain.

Outbound comment bodies lack encoding through the RichTextCodec render path that descriptions use; comment bodies must be rendered via RichTextCodec.to_wire (Cloud ADF-encoded, DC wiki-rendered) and the dedup-key codec injection migrated from _IdentityCodec to the real rendering codec.

Inbound-origin comments (carrying jira_comment_id field) may be re-pushed outbound because the outbound differ only checks body equality; the outbound differ must skip a local comment when either its local key exists in the outbound map OR it carries a jira_comment_id field (inbound-origin).
Sync is not truly append-only; edits and deletes are not prevented from being synced; only new comment creation should mirror bidirectionally, with edits and deletes never pushed or applied.

A process hard-kill between successful add_comment() and map save() loses the ID mapping, risking duplicate re-post on next pass; record_comment_id() must save() the mapping immediately (write-ahead) as a crash-durability guarantee, with the demoted body-equality test as secondary fallback.
